title: Pump: cavitation and dry running
text: Dry running or cavitation causes grinding or rattling noise, falling outlet pressure and rapid seal and bearing damage. Running dry beyond 2 minutes requires seal inspection. Check suction line, strainer and fluid level.

title: Pump: bearing failure symptoms
text: Worn bearings cause grinding noise, bearing temperature above 80 C and vibration above 7.1 mm/s. Inspect lubrication, shaft alignment and bearing play. Above 95 C stop the pump.

title: Pump: mechanical seal leakage
text: Seal leakage appears as dripping near the shaft, often after dry running or misalignment. Replace the seal if leakage exceeds 10 drops per minute.

title: Pump: motor overheating
text: Motor temperature above 90 C indicates overload, blocked ventilation, voltage imbalance or bearing drag. Check fan cover, supply voltage and current draw.

title: Compressor: high discharge temperature
text: Discharge temperature above 110 C suggests low oil, fouled cooler or worn valves. Check oil level, cooler fins and intake filter.

title: Compressor: low oil pressure
text: Oil pressure below 1.5 bar risks bearing damage. Check oil level, oil filter and oil pump. Below 0.8 bar shut down immediately.

title: Motor: winding overheating
text: Winding temperature above 120 C indicates overload, phase imbalance or poor cooling. Measure current on all phases and inspect cooling airflow.

title: Motor: abnormal vibration
text: Vibration above 4.5 mm/s suggests misalignment, loose mounting, unbalanced rotor or worn bearings. Check coupling alignment and foundation bolts.

title: General: restart after power loss
text: After a power cut, check phase sequence, lubrication state and that suction and discharge valves are in the correct position before judging a fault.

title: General: priority guidance
text: Urgent: safety risk or critical threshold exceeded. High: warning thresholds exceeded with active symptoms. Medium: intermittent symptoms. Low: cosmetic or monitoring only.
